messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions: celebrity_net_worth_get twice, and calculate_bmi twice.

First request: net worth of Lionel Messi in Euros. So call celebrity_net_worth_get with name "Lionel Messi", currency "EUR".

Second request: net worth of LeBron James in British Pounds. Call celebrity_net_worth_get with name "LeBron James", currency "GBP".

Third request: BMI of person weighing 85 kg, height 180 cm, unit metric. So call calculate_bmi with weight=85, height=180, unit="metric". Actually default is metric so we can omit unit but include for clarity.

Fourth request: BMI of person weighing 200 pounds, height 6 ft 2 in, unit imperial. Need to convert weight to pounds? The function expects weight in kilograms if unit metric; if unit imperial, weight in pounds and height in centimeters? Wait description: "Weight of the person in kilograms." "Height of the person in centimeters." But optional param unit chooses between 'imperial' and 'metric', default metric. If unit imperial, likely weight in pounds and height in inches? But description says still weight in kilograms and height in centimeters. That seems contradictory. However typical BMI calculation uses weight in kilograms and height in meters. For imperial, weight in pounds and height in inches. But the function signature says weight: number, height: number, unit?: string. It doesn't specify units for imperial. But we can assume weight in pounds and height in inches when unit imperial. So we need to pass weight=200, height=74 (6*12+2), unit="imperial".

Thus calls:

1. celebrity_net_worth_get({"name":"Lionel Messi","currency":"EUR"})
2. celebrity_net_worth_get({"name":"LeBron James","currency":"GBP"})
3. calculate_bmi({"weight":85,"height":180,"unit":"metric"})
4. calculate_bmi({"weight":200,"height":74,"unit":"imperial"})

We should output results after each call. We'll do sequential calls.
